speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I understand you are having trouble conceiving and experiencing discomfort during sexual activity. To help me understand your symptoms better, how long have you been trying to conceive, and would you describe the pain as sharp, burning, or aching?

speaker: Patient
text: 30-year-old female. The patient and her husband have been trying to conceive for 15 months without success. They are sexually active at least twice a week. The husband occasionally has difficulties maintaining an erection. The patient reports discomfort and pelvic floor muscle tension during attempted vaginal penetration. Diagnosed with body dysmorphic disorder three years ago. No family history of serious illness. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. No medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Dyspareunia secondary to pelvic floor muscle tension/myofascial pain syndrome. (Note: Untrusted input indicates 15 months of infertility and partner ED, but the primary complaint driving the visit is sexual discomfort; immediate workup for infertility is pending further discussion, but the clinical picture strongly suggests pelvic floor dysfunction as the primary etiology for her symptoms).
